text: {"lessons":["Selling winners in small pieces can feel good but may leave me underexposed if they keep rising; I should size trades by forward-looking risk and return, not the satisfaction of locking in gains.","Buying more after prices fall is not automatically a bargain, just as a gain over my average cost is not a reason to sell; with random price changes, past moves do not predict what comes next.","I should judge performance and risk across the whole portfolio, not each stock as a separate account: several profitable sales did not prevent my account value from falling, so diversification and disciplined allocation matter."]}
